claims.text: A 10–20 nm ALD-deposited Al2O3 layer inserted between the Zr-alloy substrate and elemental Cr coating will prevent premature coating failure.
The Al2O3 interlayer will impede Cr–Zr interdiffusion under high-temperature steam conditions.
The Al2O3 interlayer will retain protective performance under normal subcritical-water conditions.
ALD can produce a continuous and conformal 10–20 nm Al2O3 layer on the Zr-alloy cladding before Cr deposition.
The ultrathin Al2O3 barrier will adhere strongly to the substrate.
The ultrathin Al2O3 barrier will remain intact during thermal cycling.
Al2O3 is sufficiently chemically inert and thermally stable to function as the proposed interfacial barrier.
Suppressing Cr–Zr interdiffusion will prevent formation of deleterious intermetallic phases or other diffusion-related degradation.
At approximately 350°C in subcritical water, the barrier will remain intact and allow the Cr coating to provide corrosion resistance.
Relative to Cr-coated Zr alloy without a barrier, the modified cladding will exhibit significantly less Cr–Zr interdiffusion after steam exposure at approximately 1200°C for 10–100 seconds.
Reduced interdiffusion will preserve the integrity and protective function of the Cr coating during accident-relevant steam exposure.
The Al2O3 barrier will not compromise performance during 10^4 hours of subcritical-water exposure at approximately 350°C.
Approximately 350°C for 10^4 hours in subcritical water is the stated normal-operation test boundary.
Approximately 1200°C for 10–100 seconds in steam is the stated accident test boundary.
